stem: A tall adolescent with long thin limbs, a downward-and-inward dislocated lens and a history of deep-vein thromboses is found to have markedly elevated plasma homocysteine and methionine. Which enzyme deficiency underlies this inborn error?
concept: Classic homocystinuria is due to cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency (a B6-dependent enzyme), raising homocysteine and methionine and causing a marfanoid habitus, ectopia lentis (typically downward), thromboembolism and intellectual disability. It is distinguished from Marfan syndrome (upward lens dislocation, normal homocysteine); some patients respond to high-dose pyridoxine.
subject: Biochemistry
